Let me share a quick update on our Sprint progress. We finished profiling the local inference pipeline and verified that our sliding window keeps memory usage stable below the target threshold. However, we noticed minor latency fluctuations when multiple browser tabs run web RTC call simultaneously, so we are preparing a rollback strategy and finalizing the acceptance criteria before our release demo.

Before we lock the architecture for the prototype, I want to walk through three critical risks we discovered during testing. First, if the local speech recognition buffer grows unbounded over a 60-minute meeting, memory consumption can spike unexpectedly and degrade video call frame rates. Second, network dependent speech services introduce unpredictable delays above 500 milliseconds, breaking the natural conversational rhythm. Third, speakers often pause briefly mid-sentence while searching for precise domain terminology, so keeping prefix pinning active ensures the model prioritizes project vocabulary without duplicating context memory.
